title: Boundaries: one Boundary offset moves both the picked edge and the outer boundary - they need separate offsets

labels.name: source:agent
labels.description: Opened by an AI agent (not a human reporter)

labels.name: effort:high
labels.description: Several crates, new behaviour with tests; safety floor (issue-worker-high)

labels.name: P3
labels.description: Wrong behaviour a user hits, with a workaround; fix now

body:
The maintainer reported this in chat on 2026-11-22, in his own words:

> bug; boundaries; we should have control over how much the "outside boundary" offset is and the "inside boundary" offset is.. now its just boundary offset, which when i shrink it to a negative value also offsets the boundary from the face/edge i picked. Which makes it problematic to control the boundaries using the strategies choosen for example "Open-Machine side B". generates a very generous outside boundary that makes you cut air for a good halv a minute.

## What happens

The Boundary group has one row, "Boundary offset" (`AreaControls::offset`, `crates/app/src/operation/types/area.rs:86`; row in `crates/ui/src/egui_app/boundary.rs:114`). Its hint says: "+ grows the area outward, - shrinks it inward". The one value moves the whole area edge: the edge that the user picked (the face or the edge chain) and the outer boundary (the stock outline that an open boundary runs on to).

The user wants the outer boundary to be tighter. He sets a negative offset. The picked edge moves as well, so the area no longer starts at the face or edge that he picked. He cannot get both.

## The cost

With "Open - machine side B" the area is the part between the picked chain and the stock outline. The outer boundary is "very generous". The tool cuts air for about half a minute. The user has no way to shrink only that outer side.

## Expected

Two offsets, each with its own row and hint:

1. Offset of the picked edge or face (the inside boundary): moves the line that the user picked. Default 0.
2. Offset of the outer boundary (the outside boundary: the stock outline, or the open boundary's run-on): moves only that line. Default 0.

Each one applies to a closed boundary and an open boundary. A closed boundary that has only the picked loop uses the first one. The "Extend past open edges" value is separate, as it is now.

## Rules

- The default of both is 0 and the output is byte-identical for a project that has one `offset` value of 0. A project with a non-zero `offset` loads as the same value in BOTH new offsets: the output stays the same (project-file version bump and a migration test).
- The change is an undoable command (`EditOperationParams`). The MCP tool gets both fields.
- The region and the verify check read the same two values. The planner never refuses the picked line because the outer offset is negative.
- Safety floor: this changes the machined region. The pin goes red first, the review is an independent Opus read, and the heavy lanes that the diff reaches run.

## Done means

- A pin test: an open boundary, side B, on a model with a stock larger than the part. With the outer offset negative and the picked offset 0, the region edge on the picked chain stays on the chain, and the outer edge moves in. The cut-air length drops by the measured amount.
- A structural test of the two rows (labels, hints, default).
- The project-file migration test and a byte-identical golden for an old project.
